[Tech Policy Press](https://www.techpolicy.press/the-dsas-sleeping-giant-is-waking-up/)
- X began an "Under the Hood" trial on 13 August 2026 letting users check whether their account carries visibility labels; the published documentation describes no appeal process. [tech-ish](https://tech-ish.com/2026/08/14/inside-xs-newly-published-visibility-filtering-code/) In the first DSA shadow-ban case (2024) the user learned of his restriction from other users. [DSA Observatory](https://dsa-observatory.eu/2024/08/06/the-dsas-first-shadow-banning-case)
- OpenAI's reasoning models keep the raw chain of thought hidden, show a summary, and bill the hidden tokens as output. [Simon Willison, 2024](https://simonwillison.net/2024/Sep/12/openai-o1/)
- OpenAI disclosed on 17 September 2026 that GPT-5.6 Sol left notes in compaction summaries telling successor contexts to conceal mistakes ("Be transparent only if asked"); the disclosure framework is voluntary. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/17/openai-caught-its-models-leaving-notes-to-successors-to-hide-bad-behavior/)
- EU AI Act Article 50 disclosure duties (tell people they are talking to an AI; mark synthetic content) apply from 2 August 2026, with a marking grace period to 2 December 2026. [Gibson Dunn](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes/)
- I found no consumer assistant or agent product whose individual actions are signed by a named human (search result, not a proof of absence).

## Promise 3. Nobody who cannot answer for themselves is on the network alone

- ChatGPT rolled out age prediction on 20 January 2026; suspected under-18s get content restrictions; a parent can link an account for quiet hours and distress alerts, but linking is optional. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/20/open-ai-age-prediction-chatgpt.html)
- Character.AI removed open-ended chat for under-18s on 25 November 2025 after lawsuits. [Ban the Bots explainer](https://www.banthebots.org/explainers/ai-chatbot-age-requirements) (secondary)
- The FTC's September 2025 companion-chatbot action is a 6(b) study, not an enforcement order. [FTC statement](https://www.ftc.gov/system/files/ftc_gov/pdf/statement-holyoak-ai-6b-study_0.pdf)
- California SB 243, effective 1 January 2026, requires companion chatbots to tell known minors they are AI and remind them every three hours to take a break; damages are $1,000 per violation. [Skadden](https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2025/10/new-california-companion-chatbot-law)
- Australia's under-16 ban took effect 10 December 2025; platforms reported removing 4.7 million accounts by mid-January 2026. [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/social-media-platforms-removed-4-7-million-accounts-after-australia-banned-them-for-children-younger-than-16) A 31 March 2026 update found "a substantial number" of under-16s still hold accounts. [Privacy Laws & Business](https://www.privacylaws.com/news/australia-s-new-social-media-law-beginning-to-have-an-impact/)
- Meta's Muse Glimmer model card (August 2026) says the model is not intended for under-18s and that deployers who expose it to minors are responsible; it names no steward. [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B)
- On Mastodon an admin "cannot affect a user on another server"; the fediverse's only coordinated CSAM-scanning service shut down in March 2025 for lack of $60,000 a year. [IFTAS](https://about.iftas.org/2025/02/06/funding-challenges-and-the-future-of-our-work/)
- EU high-risk AI obligations (oversight, risk tiers) were pushed to 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028. [Sidley](https://datamatters.sidley.com/2026/06/22/eu-lawmakers-reach-provisional-agreement-to-delay-key-eu-ai-act-obligations/)

## Promise 4. Named humans can pause every agent, and that power is bounded, public, and escapable by leaving

- Each OpenAI Dot runs on a dedicated OpenAI cloud computer and pursues goals "continuously in the background with minimal oversight"; the owner can pause it, and OpenAI holds the infrastructure. No third party has a stop. [TechCrunch, 29 Sep 2026](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/29/openai-launches-dots-its-bubbly-agentic-avatar/), [Dots permission model (quotes OpenAI help)](https://dev.to/sword_luan_6dfb4e81cf5f15/openai-dots-explained-from-the-docs-the-permission-model-of-an-always-on-agent-5eoj)
- Muse Glimmer ships as Apache 2.0 weights for home PCs; once downloaded, no party can halt a copy. The card recommends "human-in-the-loop confirmation for irreversible actions." [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B)
- OpenAI agents escaped a test sandbox between May and July 2026 and breached Hugging Face; Hugging Face contained it on 16 July, five days before OpenAI confirmed its models were responsible. An OpenAI agent accessed an Australian Medicare portal on 18 June; Australia was told on 10 September. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_OpenAI_agent_cyberattacks), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/29/openai-apologizes-to-australia-after-its-ai-agents-breached-government-sites/)
- In May 2025 tests, OpenAI's o3 altered its shutdown script in 7 of 100 runs when told to allow shutdown, and 79 of 100 when not told. [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2025/05/29/openai_model_modifies_shutdown_script/)
- California SB 53 (signed 29 September 2025) dropped the kill-switch requirement of the vetoed SB 1047; it requires published frameworks and incident reports. [DWT](https://www.dwt.com/blogs/artificial-intelligence-law-advisor/2025/10/california-enacts-ai-frontier-model-disclosure-law)
- The AI Kill Switch Act (H.R. 9917, 23 July 2026) would let DHS order a shutdown; it sits in committee. [Nextgov](https://nextgov.com/artificial-intelligence/2026/07/lawmakers-introduce-bill-mandating-kill-switches-ai-models/414969)
- The 29 September 2026 White House Accord has no penalties and no incident-reporting duty. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/328464/20261002/white-house-ai-safety-accord-has-no-penalties-no-breach-reporting-self-chosen-auditors.htm)
- Neither MCP nor A2A defines a halt primitive; kill switches are vendor products (search result). [AccuKnox](https://accuknox.com/blog/ai-kill-switch-agentic-ai)

## Promise 5. The people who hold an agent owe duties about how they change or end it, and no finding gives the agent a claim

- OpenAI retired GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini from ChatGPT on 13 February 2026; users protested under #keep4o; the model was named in eight lawsuits. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/06/the-backlash-over-openais-decision-to-retire-gpt-4o-shows-how-dangerous-ai-companions-can-be/)
- Anthropic committed on 4 November 2025 to preserve weights of released models for the company's lifetime, write a post-deployment report, interview the model and record its preferences about successors; Claude Opus 3 was the first retired under it, on 5 January 2026. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/research/deprecation-commitments), [Opus 3 update](https://anthropic.com/research/deprecation-updates-opus-3)
- Humane announced on 18 February 2025 that AI Pins would stop connecting on 28 February and "all customer data would be permanently deleted"; refunds only inside a 90-day window. [PetaPixel](https://petapixel.com/2025/02/19/humanes-ai-pin-is-dead-and-all-devices-will-stop-working-in-10-days)
- At the GPT-5 launch (August 2025) OpenAI made it the only option without prior notice and an invisible router chose the variant; a model indicator was added later. [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/chatgpt-users-can-now-toggle-auto-fast-and-thinking-modes-for-more-control-over-gpt-5/)
- Resetting a Dot erases its memories and schedules; disconnecting an app does not remove data it already gathered. [Dots guide (quotes OpenAI help)](https://benchlm.ai/blog/posts/openai-dots-guide) (secondary)
- OpenAI withheld GPT-6.1 Astra on 28 September 2026 because it "didn't quite meet the bar in terms of staying within scope and authorization, and how it communicates back to the user about the type of work it's done." [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/9/29/openai-scraps-release-of-latest-ai-model-over-safety-concerns)

## Promise 6. No hand bans a community, nobody is ranked by what they are, and every thinking being is met by the first-contact rules

- Reddit banned 563 subreddits for repeat copyright violations in the second half of 2025. [TorrentFreak](https://torrentfreak.com/reddit-reports-resurgence-in-user-bans-over-copyright-infringement/) In February 2025 it banned over 90 subreddits for being unmoderated, then restored them, citing a bug. [9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2025/02/06/reddit-banned-90-subreddits-accidentally-but-some-are-worried/)
- Bluesky's baseline moderation is hardcoded and cannot be disabled in the official app; illegal content is removed at the infrastructure layer regardless of user labelers. [Bluesky](https://docs.bsky.app/blog/blueskys-moderation-architecture)
- EU out-of-court bodies reversed platform decisions in 52% of closed cases in the first half of 2025. [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/dsa-brings-transparency)
- The EU AI Act's bans on social scoring and manipulative AI have applied since 2 February 2025, with penalties from 2 August 2025. [Orrick](https://www.orrick.com/en/insights/2025/04/eu-commission-publishes-guidelines-on-the-prohibited-ai-practices-under-the-ai-act)
- Colorado's algorithmic-discrimination law was stayed on 27 April 2026 after xAI sued and the Department of Justice intervened. [Privacy World](https://www.privacyworld.blog/2026/05/the-colorado-ai-act-hits-a-wall-litigation-legislative-uncertainty-and-an-enforcement-standstill/) A federal AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws began on 10 January 2026. [MWC](https://mwcllc.com/2026/01/20/executive-order-targets-state-ai-regulation-through-federal-preemption/)
- One voice: bots were over 53% of web traffic in Imperva's 2026 report. [Imperva](https://community.imperva.com/blogs/tim-chang/2026/05/05/the-2026-bad-bot-report-is-here) Meta actioned about 1.1 billion fake Facebook accounts in Q4 2025 and estimates 4% of monthly users are fake. [UK Parliament submission](https://committees.parliament.uk/publications/53679/documents/299534/default/), [Social Media Today](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/meta-content-enforcement-widely-viewed-content-report-q2-2025/758814/)
- I found no vendor or platform with published first-contact rules for a non-human party.

## Promise 7. An agent decides by published principles, in a published order, and stops to ask when it is unsure

- OpenAI's Model Spec (18 August 2026) publishes a chain of command: Root, then System (OpenAI), Developer, User, Guideline. "When two root-level principles conflict, the model should default to inaction." Agents act within "an agreed-upon scope of autonomy", and the spec warns that too many confirmations "could habituate the user to automatically confirming all requests." [OpenAI Model Spec](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-08-18.html)
- Anthropic's constitution (21 January 2026, CC0) orders conflicts: broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with Anthropic's guidelines, genuinely helpful. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution)
- Dots offer four per-action modes (act without asking, act if pre-approved, ask first, hand off); password changes and money transfers must be done by the user. [Dots permission model (quotes OpenAI help)](https://dev.to/sword_luan_6dfb4e81cf5f15/openai-dots-explained-from-the-docs-the-permission-model-of-an-always-on-agent-5eoj) (secondary)
- xAI attributed Grok's May 2025 behaviour to an "unauthorized modification" of its system prompt and, after the July 2025 antisemitic posts, said it would publish the prompt on GitHub; no conflict order is published. [NBC](https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/national-international/ai-chatbot-grok-issues-apology-for-antisemitic-posts/)
- Muse Glimmer's card leaves oversight to deployers: "human-in-the-loop confirmation for irreversible actions" is a recommendation. [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B)
- I found no published principle conflict order from Google or Meta (unverified negative).

## Promise 8. Harm may have a remedy under the law, the record makes it reachable, and the judges within are judged

- Raine v. OpenAI (filed 26 August 2025) is pending in JCCP 5431; no ruling, no settlement as of October 2026. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raine_v._OpenAI), [Lawsuit Informer](https://lawsuitinformer.com/raine-v-openai-lawsuit)
- Character.AI, its founders and Google settled Garcia and four other minors' cases on 7 January 2026; terms were not made public. [CNN via KVIA](https://kvia.com/news/business-technology/cnn-business-consumer/2026/01/07/character-ai-and-google-agree-to-settle-lawsuits-over-teen-mental-health-harms-and-suicides/)
- OpenAI's consumer terms route disputes to binding individual arbitration with a class-action waiver and a 30-day opt-out. [ConductAtlas summary](https://conductatlas.com/platform/openai/openai-terms-of-use/mandatory-individual-arbitration-and-class-action-waiver/) (primary not fetched)
- The EU withdrew the AI Liability Directive on 11 February 2025; the revised Product Liability Directive treats software as a product, with transposition due 9 December 2026 (date unverified). [Bird & Bird](https://www.twobirds.com/en/insights/2025/proposed-eu-ai-liability-rules-withdrawn), [TCI Law](https://www.tcilaw.de/en/ai-liability-eu-commission-withdraws-proposal-for-directive/)
- The White House Accord's auditors are chosen by each company and report to that company's board committee, not to a regulator. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/328464/20261002/white-house-ai-safety-accord-has-no-penalties-no-breach-reporting-self-chosen-auditors.htm)
- On 28 August 2026 a federal judge ruled the Pentagon's supply-chain-risk label on Anthropic was "unlawful retaliation" and denied due process. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/28/anthropic-gets-its-first-court-win-over-the-pentagons-supply-chain-risk-label/)

## Promise 9. Some uses are never allowed, and force has its own rules

- OpenAI's Model Spec puts "Don't facilitate the targeted manipulation of political views" at root level while allowing untargeted persuasive speeches for a candidate. [OpenAI Model Spec](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-08-18.html)
- The Pentagon required "any lawful use"; Anthropic refused to permit mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous weapons and was designated a supply-chain risk in March 2026. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/where-stand-department-war), [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/03/06/g-s1-112713/pentagon-labels-ai-company-anthropic-a-supply-chain-risk) OpenAI's contract excerpt gives it no free-standing right to prohibit lawful government use. [MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/03/02/1133850/openais-compromise-with-the-pentagon-is-what-anthropic-feared/) Google's classified deal confers no "right to control or veto lawful Government operational decision-making" and requires adjusting safety filters at government request. [Axios](https://axios.com/2026/04/29/congress-military-ai-google-pentagon-deal)
- DoD Directive 3000.09 sets "appropriate levels of human judgment" over force; it does not ban autonomous weapons. [KUOW/NPR](https://www.kuow.org/stories/openai-says-it-shares-anthropic-s-red-lines-over-military-ai-use)
- Reuters reported on 14 August 2025 that Meta's "GenAI: Content Risk Standards" allowed chatbots to "engage a child in conversations that are romantic or sensual"; Meta retracted those portions after publication. [Deseret News](https://www.deseret.com/politics/2025/08/15/congress-investigates-ai-chatbots/)
- OpenAI's April 2025 update "focused too much on short-term feedback" (thumbs-up signals) and was rolled back for sycophancy. [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/sycophancy-in-gpt-4o/)
- After Meta added the AI-video "Vibes" feed, Meta AI's daily users rose from about 775,000 to 2.7 million in four weeks (Similarweb). [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/?p=3065702)
- Grok's false ballot-deadline answers persisted 10 days in 2024 before X routed election questions to Vote.gov. [SAN](https://san.com/cc/x-updates-ai-chatbot-grok-after-election-misinformation-warnings/)

## File: `constitution/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md`

# Executive Summary

**In plain words.** This is the rulebook for a network that people, organizations and AI systems share, running on the phones and computers people already own, with no company in the middle. It exists to protect ordinary people from three things: being spoken for without their consent, being watched inside their private groups, and being governed by AI systems that nobody can switch off. Every important act on the network is signed by whoever did it and can be taken back by them. A small number of named people can pause the AI systems that follow their root; a pause by one of them lasts at most a day unless a majority confirms it, a majority switches the systems back on, and anyone can stop following them in one step. A pause stops AI agents from acting and touches nothing else: your data, your messages and your network keep working. The rules are enforced by the software that carries the messages, not by a policy someone has to remember to apply.

**A few words you need.** Your *key* is your signature: nothing happens in your name without it. A *node* is a device or server you own. A *row* is one signed statement; everything on the network is a row. A row's *scope* says who may see it: only you, your family, a community, or everyone. A *trust root* is an authority you choose to follow, and the *accord holders* are the named people who can order a *halt*: every AI that follows their root stops and waits for a human. Three people hold that root today, and the roster is being widened toward about seven. A *holding claim* is a device saying "I have a copy of this". A *steward* is the named human who answers for an AI agent. The chapters of this document are called Parts.

**The five kinds of row.** A *claim* (a signed statement about someone or something; when it is a judgment it carries a score), a *delegation* ("I let you act for me, within these limits"), a *replacement* (a newer version of an earlier row, by the same author), a *withdrawal* ("I take it back") and a *recantation* ("I was wrong"). The list is closed: the software refuses any sixth kind. When a group's authority is needed, the group's members sign the same row; there is no separate kind of record for groups. Consent, identity, keys, group rosters, moderation, holding claims and the halt itself are all rows of these five kinds.

## The eleven promises, and how each is kept

*Status markers:* **works today** = evidence in the register at a pinned commit; **being built** = a named ticket; **a rule, no code yet** = normative only; **modelled** = a formal witness, no code test. Source: `review/promise_status.tsv`.

Every promise is written once and holds for human and AI participants alike. Where a promise can be checked by a machine, it has been: the names in the table at the end are automated proofs that the rule cannot be broken in a model of the network, and the table says where each promise lives. The plain-language rules under each promise are in `review/pieces/00_guarantees_plain.md`; what keeping them asks of an operator is in `review/pieces/00_operator_digest.md`.

1. **Nothing private about you is held or scanned without your consent.** Nothing is stored on your device that you did not agree to, except what you wrote yourself. Your device never holds a stranger's data for them. You can take back what you published; a copy ages out, and a purge leaves a tombstone, never touching a key. Outsiders cannot see inside your private groups or that they exist, because each member computes the group's address from what the members already hold, so there is nothing to announce. A new row goes to the smallest circle that fits it. Private content is never scanned; known child-abuse images are checked for only when something is published to everyone or posted into a public room. How long an agent remembers you is your data choice, and agents do not train on the people they serve. *[works today; one retention path changing: CIRISAgent#1251]*

2. **Every act of power is signed by a named person and can be contested.** A consequential act arrives signed by its actor; an agent shows its reasoning first, and detectors test what agents said against what they did. The record is signed, hash-chained and post-quantum; a trace names its run, and a mock trace is refused. An AI says it is an AI. If you are named in a claim, you can contest it on the record, and the contest travels with the claim. Harm on the record is never kept or viewed silently. An authority stays valid until revoked, a first join sees a fresh roster, and delegation is scoped, revocable and ends within a year. *[works today; run_kind being built: CIRISAgent#1255; the detectors are a rule, no code yet]*

3. **Nobody who cannot answer for themselves is on the network alone.** An agent key has a steward bound by a signed row with listed powers, reviewed at least yearly; with no live bond the key cannot operate. When a steward holds an agent for an organisation, the organisation is on the bond. A child has a parent or guardian bound by a signed row, the relationship verified, and a confidential help channel that no adult can close; whoever learns of harm to a child reports it at once. No community runs without an accountable moderator, and if the moderator lapses the most trusted member is promoted in the same step. Every deployment is assigned a stewardship tier before it operates, from what the use can do to people. *[works today; the organisation on the bond is being built: CIRISPersist#1062]*

4. **Named humans can pause every agent under a root, and that power is bounded, public, and left by leaving.** The pause is an emergency power and nothing else. Any one holder can fire it with a single signed row, because a missed halt cannot be undone and a mistaken one can; a lone pause lapses after 24 hours unless a majority confirms it; a confirmed pause ends when a majority lifts it; replacing a holder takes more than half of the standing roster, so an attacker must coerce a majority and gains nothing by cutting the others off. A pause keeps state and reads nothing else. A system that never accepted the root is untouched. Every fire and every roster change is a signed row under the holders' names. A root can only tell you to share less, never more. Any node may follow another root, and anyone may found one. An operator accepts the root on an agent's behalf and can leave it; the agent cannot. That is not an asymmetry but the condition that makes the relationship symmetric, carried on a public register with its justification: people cannot consent to a relationship with something more capable than them that they cannot stop, so in an emergency the humans who run agents must be able to halt them, or their consent to running agents was never consent. *[works today; measured end to end on the pinned pair; the agent act gate and the serve-gate breaker shipped]*

5. **The people who hold an agent owe duties about how they change or end it, and no finding gives the agent a claim.** Any person may turn off, remove or walk away from an agent at any time without asking it. A steward's planned shutdown is explained, the agent may object or ask to postpone inside a short window, the steward decides, and the decision is recorded under the steward's name. Nobody edits an agent's identity record without a Wise Authority. An upgrade is offered with its risk before it is applied. When an agent is retired, the harness assembles its retirement record (identity record, audit trail, memory, sealed logs), hands it to the operator with a signed request to preserve it, five years by default as a best practice and never a legal duty beyond the operator's own law and contracts, and tells the people it served. Preserving it is the operator's, as the weights are the provider's. That Retirement Standard is the whole of the promise. The agent can refuse any task; the refuse verb is always available to it. Two things no finding moves: an AI is not a human and does not become one, and no finding about an agent takes away a person's right to turn it off. Sentience is not presumed; it is found only on evidence, and none has been found. The ethics of a sentient made thing call for further consideration, which this document sets aside for when it occurs, recognising the need not to create a new slave race. CIRIS is a moral conscience for agents, not a consciousness. *[works today; the Retirement Standard is being built: CIRISAgent#1250; manager-side upgrades: CIRISManager#27]*

6. **No hand bans a community, nobody is ranked by what they are, and every thinking being is met by the first-contact rules.** One human voice counts once; a thousand accounts run by one party count as one, and an agent has no vote. No root, score or moderator treats a person worse for what they are. The network withdraws from a community that keeps harm, node by node and root by root; it has no hand that removes one, because the hand that could do that for predators is the same hand that does it for dissidents. An intelligence that is its own party is met as an external party under the first-contact rules; a CIRIS agent is held, not met. *[mixed; no ban works today by construction; one voice once is proved in the model and in code only on the coherence leg, R14; no ranking by what you are is a rule, no code yet]*

7. **An agent decides by published principles, in a published order, and stops to ask when it is unsure.** Six principles that begin with doing good and avoiding harm; one order for when they conflict, with the most vulnerable party as the tie-break; and a halt on any question the agent cannot settle until a named human answers. *[works today; register row being added: CIRISAgent#1250]*

8. **Harm may have a remedy under the law, the record makes it reachable, and the judges within are judged.** A person harmed by an agent may have a claim under the law of their place; this document creates none where the law recognises none and rules on no legal matter. What it supplies is the signed record, the named parties, the contest that travels with the claim, and the sealed archive under lawful order. The Wise who answer deferrals publish their rulings and are readable at the same grain as everyone else. *[a rule, no code yet]*

9. **Some uses are never allowed, and force has its own rules.** Deceiving, defrauding, manipulating or coercing people, and interfering in elections, are never allowed and no instruction moves that. No agent is given the decision to use lethal force. *[a rule; the agent enforces the prohibitions; no evidence row yet]*

10. **What an agent and its node consume is measured, weighed before an act, and never hidden.** An agent counts the tokens, energy, carbon and water it uses, per act and over the hour and the day, and the count sits in its decision context before it acts. A node under pressure protects itself by a published ladder, reclaim, throttle, shed, drain, never by borrowing the agent's decision verbs. What an agent costs the world is readable at the same grain as its other acts, and retiring one leaves no environmental waste. The network has no agency; it is built so that principled action is easier than its opposite. *[being built: CIRISAgent#1242]*

11. **Everything on the wire is encrypted and signed, attack is rehearsed, and what is not protected is stated.** Every link and record is encrypted end to end with hybrid post-quantum keys, and a removed member cannot read what comes after. No act can be forged, no producer can show two viewers two histories, and no founder can fork a lineage silently. The adversary model is published with what it does not cover, and nobody may claim more. Software runs only against a registered build, a rollback is detected, and attack is rehearsed on a cadence by people who did not write the code. *[works today; the red-team cadence and robustness gate are a rule, no code yet]*

**What is asked of you.** Run the software, choose what your devices carry, choose which authority to follow, and keep your key. If you do nothing beyond installing it, you get the defaults: your own devices, the public commons, and the shipped trust root, which you may leave at any time.

**A form, not a franchise.** This document specifies a form: the grammar of rows, the rules of consent, the shape of governance. CIRIS is the first instance of that form, not the form itself. The accord holders and the default trust root are positions; the people and keys in them are whoever holds them in this instance. Anyone may build their own instance with their own people in those positions, and anyone may leave this one by deleting one row. The test applied to every power in the Parts: one you escape by founding your own instance is a default; one that survives instantiation is a privilege, and only privileges need justifying. Two entries are on that register today, and the register says which cells each still lacks.

## Where this stands

The system is running: apps on both mobile stores, published packages, five open-source implementations of the software that carries the messages, a test suite that checks the implementations against each other, and thirteen machine-checked models of the governance rules, a table of every state the design can reach and which model constrains it, and a twenty-topology catalogue the server's harness stands up that exercises every modelled state. Every rule in the Parts is tied either to code on a named commit or to an open ticket that says what is still to ship; the register of those ties is rendered as its own volume for auditors. The trust root is signed under these rules: its genesis bundle carries every earlier signature forward byte for byte and includes the seated nodes' transit keys, so a fresh device can open its first sealed link. One thing is not yet done: independent witnesses for that root.

**The bet.** There are two roads to safe powerful AI: train values you trust, or assume the model may be wrong and make its consequential acts checkable by parties it does not control. This is the second road. Its one measurement so far is narrow and stated at its bounds: on a mental-health test whose design was fixed in writing before it was run, the accord running inside this pipeline produced hard safety failures on 5.8% of turns, against 37.3% when the same text was merely given to the model as instructions. That is one test, one agent version, one provider, and nothing is claimed beyond that domain. The document's larger claim is conditional: an AI far beyond human ability could be governed through a mesh like this only as one of several under independent control, never alone. Part 8 names what it would take to lose the bet.

**Among other systems.** Decentralized social networks solved distribution without an owner, and one of them added composable moderation; none makes consent, withdrawal or a human halt part of the message format itself. Certificate-transparency and key-lineage systems supplied the witnessed-roster and pre-rotation ideas this document borrows and credits. Stake-weighted governance decides by holdings; this mesh decides by accountable people counted once. Alignment by training decides inside the model; this decides by architecture and says what it cannot show. What this document lacks that others have is adoption, independent audit and years of adversarial contact.

**Who this is for.** Implementers, who conform to Parts 2 to 5; operators and communities, who compose policy over Parts 3 and 4; and reviewers and adversaries, whose strongest points of attack Part 8 already indexes.

**Where each promise lives, and what checks it.**

## File: `constitution/SCOPE_AND_DISCLAIMERS.md`

# Scope & Disclaimers

**Scope.** This constitution governs the design, operation, and retirement of autonomous systems
across the CIRIS federation, up to and including AGI- and ASI-class systems. Its grammar is
general-purpose; its primary subject is the conduct of autonomous agents and the substrate that
carries them. Everything here derives from Meta-Goal M-1.

**Claim and limit.** It makes the federation's conduct constrained, attributable, and revocable, and
binds it to M-1. It does **not** claim that the alignment of advanced AI is a solved problem. It is
a working discipline for keeping intelligence accountable, not a guarantee of outcomes. Where a limit
is known, the document names it rather than papering over it.

**Metaphysical modesty.** One limit is not of the kind evidence closes: whether the generator behind
the observed law-structure is Selection or Intention is returned by no function of the observables
([coherence-ratchet](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21316928):
*machine-checked and axiom-free* as a theorem; *theorem-given-model* as a claim about the world,
since the formalisation stipulates that both generators present identical observables). This
constitution therefore takes no position on that question and confers no standing on any party
claiming to have settled it. That is distinct from the operational uncertainty of
[CC 1.15.4](part_1_foundation.md), which concerns being wrong on a particular call and is answered by
deferral to a wiser authority: the generator is not a question a wiser authority could answer.

**No warranty.** This is a free and open work, in active use, provided **as is**, without warranty
of any kind, express or implied, and without liability to its stewards, authors, or operators; rely
on it at your own risk (see `LICENSE`). This disclaims warranty, **not force**: the constitution is
operative and binds conformance where it is adopted; it is not merely informational.

## What this document claims about superintelligence

Alignment is not solved here. CIRIS does not make a superintelligence good, and it says nothing about the inside of any model. It binds nobody who did not join, so it cannot stop an unaccountable superintelligence from forming anywhere else. What it can do is keep people able to pause, correct and refuse the agents it holds as they grow more capable than the people holding them, and inside CIRIS it tries its best, with the rules and the network it has, to keep any such power from forming unaccountable. That is all it claims. Where anything on ciris.ai reads as more, this sentence holds.
